Can you explain the main options in simple terms?
Absolutely! Here's a simple breakdown of the main spirit categories:
Whiskey — The broad family that includes several types:
Bourbon: American whiskey made with at least 51% corn, giving it a sweet, warm flavor with notes of vanilla, caramel, and spice. It's aged in new charred oak barrels. Great for beginners!
Scotch: Whisky from Scotland, often smoky and complex
Rye: Spicier, drier whiskey made primarily from rye grain
Tequila — Made from agave plants in Mexico, ranges from smooth and citrusy (blanco) to rich and oaky (añejo)
Rum — Made from sugarcane or molasses, can be light and mixable or dark and sipping-worthy
Vodka — Clean, neutral spirit that's versatile for cocktails
Gin — Flavored with botanicals (especially juniper), aromatic and great in cocktails
We carry over 20,000 spirits from around the world, from well-known classics to rare craft bottles.
What sounds most appealing to you? Are you drawn to something sweet and smooth (bourbon), something you can mix easily (vodka/gin), or something more adventurous?

Is there anything else a beginner needs to get started?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
Good question! The great news is you don't need much to get started — bourbon is pretty simple. Here's what you need to know:
What you absolutely need:
The bourbon itself (like that Maker's Mark we discussed)
A glass — any regular glass works fine to start! You probably have something at home already.
How to drink it as a beginner:
There are three easy ways to enjoy bourbon:
Neat (just bourbon, no ice) — best for tasting the full flavor
On the rocks (over ice) — refreshing and slightly mellows the alcohol. Pro tip: use big ice cubes — they melt slower so your bourbon stays less watered down.
With a splash of water — this actually releases flavors and softens the alcohol punch, making it easier for beginners.
Optional upgrade:
If you want to enhance the experience, a proper whiskey glass helps. We have a Flaviar x Highland Park Whisky Tumbler for $14.99 — but honestly, start with what you have at home first!

How do I use it properly the very first time?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
Great question! Here's exactly how to taste your Maker's Mark for the first time:
Step 1: Pour & Prepare
Pour about 1-2 ounces into a glass. For your first time, I recommend adding 2-3 ice cubes — this chills it and makes it smoother and easier to drink.
Step 2: Smell First (Don't Skip This!)
Before you sip, gently bring the glass up to your nose — don't rush! You don't want to overwhelm your nose. Take your nose away after each sniff and repeat. Trust the first thing you smell — it might be vanilla, caramel, or something sweet. This is half the experience!
Step 3: Take a Small Sip
Take a small sip and let it sit on your tongue for a moment before swallowing. Don't gulp it! Notice the flavors — sweet, warm, maybe a little spice.
Step 4: Adjust to Your Taste
Too strong? Add a splash of water — this actually releases more flavors and softens the alcohol.
Want it colder? Add more ice
Enjoying it? Take your time between sips
Pro Tips:
Have water nearby to cleanse your palate
Don't feel pressured to drink it fast — bourbon is meant to be savored
There's no "wrong" way — if you prefer it with more ice or water, that's perfectly fine!
The goal is to enjoy it and discover what you like. Maker's Mark is forgiving and smooth, so it's perfect for experimenting. Cheers to your first bourbon experience! 🥃
